conventions.page: 1-based page index of the PDF (printed_page = the number printed in the footer, if any)
conventions.values: printed strings exactly as in the text layer (words of one cell joined by one space); empty string = blank cell. Units as printed (mostly inches; some ORFS / Flange tables are mm).
conventions.columns: key = printed header text (multi-line headers joined top to bottom with a space); letter = drawing letter when the header starts with one; the part-number column is not in columns (pn_header)
conventions.continued_from_page: set when the table has no heading of its own: it continues the previous table in reading order (series/title inherited)
conventions.line_y: baseline of the row in PDF points from the top of the page
conventions.unlabeled columns: '(no header)' / '(no header) after <key>' = a printed column without header text (e.g. 'Steel Forged', or K2 thread sizes in Flange 1967-61)
conventions.duplicate headers: a header printed twice in one table keeps its text, later ones get ' #2', ' #3' (e.g. 'M.M.' millimetre columns); 'printed' holds the header text
conventions.verified: table["verified"] = true when its page was page-checked (image + text layer) in a verify chunk that did not fail and no correction on it is unchecked / unmatched; table["corrected_from"] / row["corrected_from"] = the parsed value before a correction

known_limitations: Tables without a PART NO./Item column are not parsed (Hosetail p2 thread chart, p3 ferrule compatibility matrix); they are listed in page_warnings.
Printed typos are kept as printed (e.g. heading "05010801" over 0801-06-04, 1930-61-24-24 inside the 1929-61 table, L "23620", "136/16-16", "5/15", "2.2252"); only structural ones are warned.
Units are as printed; the parser does not mark metric tables (ORFS FS7210/FS7215 lengths and hexes, 'M.M.' columns) beyond their header text.
letter/meaning are a heuristic split of the printed header; key is the authoritative printed text.
A table with no heading above it inherits series/title from the previous table in reading order (page, left column, right column); every such link is checked for an identical header.

It has two matrices, each with Hose ID rows Inches/Dash/DN from 3/16 (-3, 5) to 2 (-32, 50), 11 rows. Matrix 1 (Non Skive) has columns PF3 (1 Wire 853 1SN / R1AT), PF3/PF11 (853 2SN / R2AT), PF17 (857 1SC), PF3 (857 2SC / R17/R19), PF4 (854 2TE), PF4/PF2 (854 3TE), PF7 (PTFE-T1 R14), PF9 (PTFE-W1 Convoluted), PF8 (Thermoplastic 855 R7) and 77 filled cells. Matrix 2 has columns PF1, PF2, PF5 (External Skive) and PFI-4SH, PFI-R13, PFI-R15 (Ext. & Int. Skive) and 43 filled cells. That makes 120 D-number cells (92 unique), all ferrule part numbers.

Neither matrix has a PART NO./Item column, and there are no fitting dimension rows. The page is listed in page_warnings and known_limitations, and catalog_parsed.json correctly has no table for p3. No fitting row is missing or wrong.

corrections_applied.verdict_note: I checked the 300 dpi crop (verify/png2/ht_p15_joiner_heading.png) and the span layer. The heading prints 'Hose Joiner' twice: once in black (Gotham-Black, y 419) and once in grey (Gotham-Bold, colour 0x939598, y 432). The grey line sits where the series code normally goes, as with HT-TW-STRT just above it. So the series 'Hose Joiner' is right and the title should be just 'Hose Joiner', not 'Hose Joiner / Hose Joiner'. This is cosmetic only. I re-checked all 10 rows on the crop (ht_p15_joiner_table.png), D208156 1/4 to D208163 2, and both columns match the parse. One small correction to the note: HOSETAIL-p019-t02 is also an HT table, and its title also has the code line appended ('Hose Tail-Code 62 Interlock-45 / HINT CD62-45'). That page is outside p9-16, so the 'every other HT table' claim holds within the checked range but not catalog-wide.
corrections_applied.action: table title: 'Hose Joiner / Hose Joiner' -> 'Hose Joiner'

corrections_applied.note: Table HOSETAIL-p019-t02 (rows D208402-D208410). The grey series code is printed with a space, 'HINT CD62-45'. The text layer has two words, 'HINT' + 'CD62-45'. Every sister heading uses a hyphen (HINT-CD62-STRT, HINT-CD62-90). Cause: the Hosetail code regex in tools/catalog/parse_brennan_catalog.py line 268 rejects the space, so the black name line became the series. All rows and cells of this table are correct.
corrections_applied.verdict_note: Hosetail p19, table HOSETAIL-p019-t02. The 300 dpi crop (verify/png2/hose_p19_t02_title.png) shows the grey code line printed as 'HINT CD62-45' with a space. The text layer has one grey span (0x939598, Gotham-Bold 10pt) 'HINT CD62-45', which splits into the words 'HINT' + 'CD62-45'. The sister heading HINT-CD62-90 on the same page is printed with a hyphen (hose_p19_t03_title.png). parse_brennan_catalog.py line 268 uses the regex [A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9/\-]*, which rejects the space, so the series fell back to the black name. The series should be the grey code. Rows D208402-D208410 (Hose I.D. / CD 62) match the print.
